views.label: Sizes that are facts
views.note: A mains period of 60 samples is a fact. Rounding it up to 64 and filling with zeros moves every bin off the frequency that was wanted.

views.label: The trick
views.note: Rewriting k*n as (k^2 + n^2 - (k-n)^2)/2 turns the sum into a convolution, and a convolution can be done at any length.

views.label: Room for the wrap
views.note: The convolution runs to 2*size-1 places. A transform repeats for ever, thus the room must be taken before the end wraps onto the start.

views.label: Any size at all
views.note: The bins fall where the caller asked, not where the next power of two would have put them.

boundaries.label: about four times the memory of the size asked for

cards.title: What it works out
items: X[k] = sum over n of x[n] * exp(-2*pi*i*k*n/size), for ANY size
A mains period at 3000 samples a second is 60 samples, and 60 is not a power of two
A block that holds no whole period spreads the hum across every bin

cards.title: How the library gets there
items: k*n = (k^2 + n^2 - (k-n)^2)/2 turns the sum into a convolution
X[k] = conj(c[k]) * sum over n of (x[n]*conj(c[n])) * c[k-n]
The square of the index is folded by 2*size, so a large index keeps its accuracy

cards.title: What it costs you
items: The convolution needs 2*size-1 places, or the end wraps onto the start
Thus the working transform is about four times the size asked for
Take fft when the size is a choice; take this when the size is a fact
